Calcium arsenite is an inorganic arsenic compound. Inorganic arsenic compounds are generally considered highly toxic. The World Health Organization (WHO) and other regulatory bodies typically set very strict limits for arsenic compounds due to their toxicity and carcinogenic potential.

For inorganic arsenic, the provisional tolerable weekly intake (PTWI) was previously set at 15 μg/kg body weight, but this was later withdrawn as it was not considered protective enough. The Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives (JECFA) has established that for inorganic arsenic, the benchmark dose lower confidence limit for a 0.5% increased incidence of lung cancer (BMDL0.5) is 3.0 μg/kg body weight per day.

B. 0.0002 mg/kg = 0.2 μg/kg
C. 0.002 mg/kg = 2 μg/kg
D. 0.2 mg/kg = 200 μg/kg

Option A (0.000002 mg/kg or 0.002 μg/kg) is the lowest and most consistent with the extremely strict limits typically placed on arsenic compounds.
